name: 905-batchdecode-dsv2-tp8
model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2. Ungated on the Hub, 55 safetensors shards, ~470 GB of bf16 weights.
hardware: 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, ONE node. No node-external tier: no disk cache, no remote store, no router, nothing on the NIC.
parallelism: tp8 over the one node; no pipeline, data or expert parallelism. The checkpoint does not fit in fewer cards at bf16.
architecture: DeepseekV2ForCausalLM, 60 layers, hidden 5120, 128 attention heads; MoE, 160 routed + 2 shared experts; 236B total / 21B active, bf16.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup the first 15%, bounded at 1000 requests with a 2400 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, SINGLE TURN, no prefix buckets: prompts centred on 236 tokens (stdev 180, clamped 16-1024) and generations centred on 216 tokens (stdev 160, clamped 16-768), seed 42. Requests go to `/v1/completions`, the only route at this release that forwards `ignore_eos`, which is what pins generated length.
purpose: A general-purpose chat assistant on a 236B mixture-of-experts model, serving 256 concurrent short single-turn requests across eight GPUs.
launch:
# sglang server arguments for this item.
# Flat `key: value` only -- an indented block is DROPPED when this file is read, and the engine
# then starts without what the dropped key declared.

model-path: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2

# The checkpoint ships its own configuration and modeling modules.
trust-remote-code: true

tp-size: 8

disable-radix-cache: true

# 4096 is the checkpoint's native window before YaRN, and the longest possible request here is
# 1024 prompt + 768 output = 1792, so nothing is truncated. LOAD-BEARING: the checkpoint
# advertises 163840 positions, and the device-side request table scales with this value -- at the
# advertised window it alone is over a gigabyte per rank.
context-length: 4096

# The engine's own default at tp-size >= 8, written down rather than left implicit.
mem-fraction-static: 0.83

random-seed: 42
